name: GlassAppShell (app-shell subpath)
stories: none for this component (src/stories/AppChromeVisualBaseline.stories.tsx imports only GlassTopBar/GlassSidebarRail/GlassPageHeader; 1 story)
screenshots: none in certification set; recipe screenshot reports/3.2-release/recipe-screenshots/saas-admin-shell.png (recipe adds its own inline CSS overrides). The certification slug components-layout-glassappshell is the DIFFERENT root GlassAppShell from src/components/layout/GlassAppShell.tsx
material_impl: Utility class strings only (glass-bg-surface/30, glass-grid-rows-[auto_1fr_auto], glass-grid-cols-[auto_minmax(0,1fr)]). There is no Tailwind compile step in the repo (no tailwind.config, no postcss config); glass-* utilities come from hand-written src/styles/glass.css. A scripted check found 50 of the 111 class tokens used in components.tsx have NO CSS rule in src/styles or dist/styles/index.css, including every grid-template arbitrary value, glass-min-h-screen, glass-bg-surface/30, glass-rounded-xl. So the shell's grid layout and density padding are partly no-ops. It uses no shared material primitive.
a11y: No skip link and no landmark labelling of its own. The topBar, sidebar and statusBar slots are passed through as-is. The sidebar sits before main in DOM order whether it is on the left or the right, which is correct. Responsive collapse is absent.
api: forwardRef, className passthrough, slot props (topBar, sidebar, actionBar, statusBar), sidebarPlacement, density. It shares its name with the root-exported GlassAppShell (src/index.ts:72), which has a different header/sidebar/footer API. docs/app-shell/readme.md admits the clash.
ssr: "use client" (components.tsx:1) even though nothing here needs client-only code. No window access.
fake_complexity: No fakes, but the layout promise depends on CSS classes that do not exist.
target: single canonical AppShell (merge with src/components/layout/GlassAppShell.tsx) built on real CSS (a CSS module or shipped stylesheet) with responsive sidebar collapse
justification: The slot API is the right shape for a first-party app frame, and a premium shell is a natural flagship. The implementation is a class-string sketch, though. Its grid templates, min-height and surface background point to utility classes the library never ships, because there is no Tailwind compile and glass.css does not define them. Two exported components share the name GlassAppShell, and neither has an honest story. The app-shell has to own its CSS, merge with the root layout version and gain responsive behaviour before it can be a flagship.
evidence: src/index.ts:72 (root GlassAppShell is the layout version)
src/registry/recipes.ts:888 (recipe must hand-write media-query overrides for .glass-app-shell__body/.glass-sidebar-rail)

name: GlassTopBar
stories: src/stories/AppChromeVisualBaseline.stories.tsx (1 story, FullSurface; component used inside a page with inline-style frame)
material_impl: Bespoke class strings: glass-border-white/15 (undefined), glass-bg-white/8 (defined), glass-backdrop-blur-xl (defined). It does not use OptimizedGlass, LiquidGlass or createGlassStyle. The sticky, top-3, min-h-14 and rounded-xl classes are all undefined in the shipped CSS. The sticky={true} default therefore does nothing, even though the docs advertise a 'Sticky header'.
a11y: Renders a <header> (banner) with an optional <nav> that has no aria-label, so it is ambiguous next to GlassSidebarRail's nav. It has no mobile menu affordance.
api: forwardRef, className, slot props (brand, navigation, actions), sticky. The API is clean.
fake_complexity: The sticky prop is effectively fake because the CSS behind it is missing.
justification: The API is minimal and sensible. It misses the premium bar because sticky positioning, corner radius, height and border do not resolve to any CSS. It also hand-rolls a white-alpha surface instead of using the library's material system, and it overlaps three other header/toolbar components. Rebuild it as part of a single shell with real material tokens.
evidence: src/app-shell/components.tsx:108-110 (glass-min-h-14, glass-rounded-xl, glass-border-white/15, glass-sticky, glass-top-3 all undefined)

name: GlassSidebarRail
material_impl: Bespoke class strings. The active state uses sky-300 classes (glass-bg-sky-300/15, glass-border-sky-300/40, glass-text-sky-100), and none of them exist in CSS, so the active item has no visual state apart from aria-current. The focus ring classes (focus-visible:glass-ring-2, glass-ring-sky-300) are also undefined, so focus falls back to whatever global :focus-visible rule happens to apply.
motion: glass-transition-colors is undefined, so there is no motion at all.
a11y: Renders <nav aria-label='Primary navigation'> with <button aria-label> items and aria-current='page' on the active item. There are no arrow-key or roving-focus controls. Items are buttons rather than links, so they cannot carry an href and cannot be opened in a new tab. Items have no visible label or tooltip; only the first letter is shown when no icon is given. The 40px targets fall just short of 44px.
api: Data-driven items array with onSelect. It has no renderItem or asChild for router links.
fake_complexity: none
target: GlassSidebar (collapsed/rail mode) using GlassRovingFocusGroup + link polymorphism
justification: The library already has three sidebar implementations, and this one is the thinnest. Its active and focus states depend on undefined classes, so it is visually flat. It has no roving focus and cannot act as a router link. Fold it into GlassSidebar as a rail mode with real active-state material and keyboard behaviour.

name: GlassSidebarPanel
material_impl: Bespoke class strings: glass-bg-white/6, glass-backdrop-blur-xl, glass-border-white/15. The width class (glass-w-72) and corner radius (glass-rounded-xl) are undefined, so the panel has no intrinsic width.
motion: The collapse is an instant width:0 jump with no transition.
a11y: When collapsed it sets aria-hidden but not inert, so its focusable children stay in the tab order while hidden from assistive tech (an aria-hidden-focus violation). The props type is NavProps, but the element rendered is <aside>.
api: forwardRef, title, footer, collapsed. It is controlled only, with no onCollapsedChange and no toggle.
fake_complexity: The docs call it a 'Collapsible labeled aside', but it has no collapse control or animation.
justification: This is a thin aside wrapper. Its width is undefined, collapsing it leaves keyboard focus inside hidden content, and it has no story. Merge it into the canonical sidebar.

name: GlassMain
material_impl: Bespoke class strings: glass-bg-white/5, glass-border-white/12, glass-backdrop-blur-xl. It puts a full-page backdrop-filter on the main scroll container, which is costly on large scroll surfaces.
a11y: Renders a <main> landmark with no id, so the library's SkipLinks ('#main-content') cannot target it. It nests a second <main> if it is used inside GlassMobileShell.
api: forwardRef with plain main props.
fake_complexity: none
justification: This is a trivial landmark wrapper. Applying blur across the whole page is the wrong default for a scroll container, and it is incompatible with the library's own skip-link target. Keep it only as a slot of the canonical shell.

name: GlassPage
material_impl: No material. glass-max-w-7xl is undefined, so constrained={true}, the default, does nothing. That contradicts docs/app-shell/readme.md ('max width 7xl').
a11y: Neutral div.
api: forwardRef, constrained boolean.
fake_complexity: The constrained prop is a no-op because its CSS is missing.
justification: It duplicates GlassContainer, and its only feature (the max-width constraint) has no CSS behind it.

name: GlassPageHeader
screenshots: none in certification set; recipe saas-admin-shell.png
material_impl: Typography only. The eyebrow colour (glass-text-sky-200) and the leading-6 and max-w-3xl classes are undefined. The eyebrow colour is hard-coded sky with no token.
a11y: Always renders the title as an <h1>, with no 'as' or level prop, so there will be several h1s when it is used in nested pages or cards. The actions container does not wrap on narrow screens (flex justify-between plus shrink-0).
api: forwardRef, eyebrow, title, description, actions. There is no heading-level control.
fake_complexity: none
target: single PageHeader (merge with layout/GlassAppShell PageHeader) with headingLevel and responsive action wrap
justification: The component is useful and simple, but it duplicates PageHeader in the root layout. It forces an h1, does not wrap its actions on mobile, and its eyebrow uses an undefined, hard-coded sky colour.

name: GlassBreadcrumbs
material_impl: Text only, with a plain '/' separator and no material.
a11y: This is the correct pattern: nav aria-label='Breadcrumb', an <ol>, aria-current='page' on the last item and an aria-hidden separator. Links have no focus style of their own and rely on the global one. List keys are array indexes.
api: Data-only items with href. It has no link component injection for routers, no separator prop and no overflow collapse.
fake_complexity: none
justification: Its semantics are correct, but it is visually generic and duplicates the root GlassBreadcrumb. It cannot render router links. Keep the a11y pattern and merge it into a single breadcrumb.

name: GlassActionBar
material_impl: Bespoke class strings: white/5, border-white/12, backdrop-blur-xl. The corner radius (glass-rounded-xl) is undefined.
a11y: Plain div with no role='toolbar' and no arrow-key navigation, despite being an action bar.
api: forwardRef with div props only.
fake_complexity: none
justification: This is a styled div that duplicates GlassToolbar. It lacks toolbar semantics, and its radius is undefined.

name: GlassSplitPane (app-shell subpath)
screenshots: none for this version; components-layout-glasssplitpane is the root src/components/layout/GlassSplitPane.tsx
material_impl: Layout only. All four ratio classes (arbitrary grid-cols and glass-grid-rows-2) are undefined, so only the 'half' ratio (glass-grid-cols-2) does anything. The 'third' and 'two-thirds' ratios have no effect.
a11y: Neutral. There is no divider or separator role and no keyboard resizing.
api: ratio and direction. direction='vertical' silently ignores ratio. It does not collapse to a single column on mobile.
fake_complexity: It is named like a split pane but is a static two-column grid with no splitter, and most of its ratios are no-ops.
justification: It shares its name with the root export, but most of its ratios are no-ops and it has no splitter. It adds confusion and gives users nothing beyond a CSS grid. Remove it and re-export the root SplitPane from the app-shell subpath.

name: GlassResizablePanel
material_impl: Bespoke class strings; the corner radius is undefined.
a11y: Plain div with no resize handle, separator role or keyboard support.
api: minSize and maxSize are mapped to min-width and max-width. The default maxSize='1fr' is an invalid max-width value that browsers ignore.
fake_complexity: FAKE: nothing can be resized. It is a bordered div with min-width and max-width.
target: real resizable panel primitive (or the root GlassSplitPane)
justification: The name promises resizing that does not exist, its default maxSize is invalid CSS, and it has no story or test. Shipping it misleads users.

name: GlassCommandDock
material_impl: Bespoke class strings: glass-bg-white/10 and glass-backdrop-blur-2xl. The sky border (glass-border-sky-300/25) and the corner radius (rounded-2xl) are undefined.
a11y: Plain flex container; the consumer must supply the input and its label. It has no role='search' or form semantics.
api: Slots for input and actions, with children used as a fallback input.
fake_complexity: The name implies command handling, but it is only a styled row.
justification: This is a decorative wrapper whose accent border and radius never render. GlassCommandPalette already covers the command UI.

name: GlassStatusBar
material_impl: Bespoke class strings; min-h-9 and the corner radius are undefined.
a11y: Puts role='status' (an implicit polite live region) on the whole bar. Every content change, including clocks and counters, is announced. This should be opt-in.
api: forwardRef with div props. It has no option to turn the live region off.
fake_complexity: none
justification: This is a thin footer whose always-on live region announces every update. Keep it as a shell slot and make announcements opt-in.

name: GlassMobileShell
material_impl: The grid rows (glass-grid-rows-[auto_1fr_auto]), glass-min-h-screen and glass-bg-surface/30 are all undefined, so the layout reduces to a bare grid. It has no safe-area insets (env(safe-area-inset-*)), and it uses 100vh-style semantics instead of dvh.
a11y: Hard-codes an inner <main>, so a GlassMain child creates nested mains. The bottomBar has no nav semantics.
api: topBar, bottomBar, children.
fake_complexity: none
duplicates: GlassAppShell (should be responsive instead of a separate shell)
justification: A separate mobile shell signals that the main shell is not responsive. This one has no safe-area handling, its grid classes are undefined and it nests main landmarks. Make the main shell responsive instead.

name: GlassIconButton (app-shell, non-shim internal export)
material_impl: Bespoke class strings. The focus ring classes and rounded-lg are undefined.
a11y: Requires a label prop, which is mapped to aria-label (good). The target is 36px, below the 44px recommendation, and the focus ring CSS is missing.
api: forwardRef with a required label. It hard-codes type='button' before {...props}, which is correct.
fake_complexity: none
justification: It duplicates GlassButton's icon mode, has no story or docs, and does not have a shim file of its own.

name: AccessibilityProvider
screenshots: reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification/screenshots/components-accessibility-accessibilityprovider/{desktop,mobile}.png (not renderable by the viewer in this run; pixel stats show a near-white frame, mean 244, std 18, so it is low-contrast and colourless)
material_impl: No material. It wraps children in a div with overflowX:hidden. That makes the div a scroll container, which breaks position:sticky in all descendants and clips popovers that overflow sideways.
motion: With reducedMotion on, it only sets --animation-duration and --animation-delay on <html>. Only GlowingCard.tsx reads --animation-duration, so framer-motion components ignore it. detectSystemPreferences is exposed but never called automatically, so the OS prefers-reduced-motion setting is not picked up unless the consumer calls it. The function returns a cleanup that callers will lose.
a11y: Its settings are almost all no-ops. No CSS exists for .high-contrast, .large-text or [data-color-blindness]. The voiceCommands, motionControls and screenReaderOptimized flags drive no behaviour, and focusIndicators and keyboardNavigation affect only GlassFocusIndicators.
api: It has no forwardRef, which is fine for a provider. The context value is a new object on every render, so every consumer re-renders. useAccessibility falls back to a silent no-op default outside the provider. Its settings model competes with src/hooks/useAccessibility.ts, src/hooks/useAccessibilitySettings.ts and the GlassA11y config, a fourth model.
ssr: Effects guard localStorage and document access, so it is SSR-safe. The first save effect writes the defaults to localStorage before the load effect's state update applies; this is benign.
fake_complexity: High. It claims WCAG settings management, but high contrast, large text, colour blindness, voice and motion controls are inert flags.
target: single preferences provider merged with ReducedMotionProvider and the theme provider; settings must map to real CSS/token switches
justification: A real a11y preferences layer would make the library stand out. This one stores flags that nothing consumes, does not detect OS preferences automatically, and its wrapper div's overflow-x:hidden breaks sticky positioning, which matters for the app-shell. It is one of four competing settings models. Redesign it as the single source that drives data-attributes the token CSS actually responds to.

name: ContrastGuard
screenshots: reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification/screenshots/components-accessibility-contrastguard/{desktop,mobile}.png (not renderable by the viewer; pixel stats show a near-white image, mean 239)
material_impl: Uses createGlassStyle (the shared mixin) only for the demoBackdrop preview. The indicator chip has hard-coded colours (#052e16, #451a03, rgba greens and oranges).
a11y: The algorithm is not a real contrast check. The textColor default 'var(--glass-text-primary)' and any hex colour are parsed as WHITE (parseColor only handles rgb()). captureBackdrop always returns null. Fallback mode 'assumes' compliance (finalContrast = requiredRatio + 0.5). The adjustments it writes have no CSS consumers: --glass-surface-opacity on the element, --glass-adaptive-tint, --glass-adaptive-blur-multiplier and the .glass-contrast-fallback class. The minContrast prop is destructured but never used. The default 'span' wrapper is used around an <h3> in KeyboardShortcutsHelper, which is invalid nesting.
api: forwardRef via useImperativeHandle and a polymorphic 'as' prop. Its level/minContrast pair is redundant, and minContrast is ignored. TextWithContrast and HighContrastText are internal wrappers that are not root-exported.
ssr: "use client". Every instance starts a ResizeObserver and a subtree MutationObserver on its parent. stopMonitoring disconnects only the ResizeObserver, because the MutationObserver is never stored, so it leaks. A singleton observer map keyed by element is shared across instances.
fake_complexity: FAKE. The story copy says it 'measures the rendered backdrop', but sampling falls back to computed styles or a constant. Its passing verdicts come from an assumed fallback and drive no visual change.
target: token-level contrast contract (pre-computed text-on-material pairs per theme) + useLiquidGlassBackdrop sampling where real; drop runtime guard
justification: The component claims WCAG enforcement but computes against white for any CSS-variable or hex text colour, assumes success on its fallback path, and writes CSS variables nothing reads. It leaks a MutationObserver on every unmount. Runtime contrast guessing is the wrong approach for a premium system. Guarantee contrast at token level, and use the existing LiquidGlassMaterial backdrop sampling where adaptive behaviour is genuinely needed.

name: GlassA11y
stories: src/components/accessibility/GlassA11y.stories.tsx (6: GlassKeyboardNav, GlassMotionControls, Default, TestingMode, HighContrast, Minimal)
tests: src/components/accessibility/GlassA11y.test.tsx (smoke, axe, aria-label, compact, relative flow, snapshot)
screenshots: reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification/screenshots/components-accessibility-glassa11y/{desktop,mobile}.png (not renderable by the viewer; near-white, mean 242). The story injects about 100 lines of !important CSS that overrides the component's surfaces, buttons and colours, so the screenshot does not represent the shipped component.
material_impl: A mix of glass-foundation-complete and glass-surface-* classes, many UNPREFIXED Tailwind classes (p-2, rounded-lg, bg-white/60, text-gray-900, focus:ring-gray-400, translate-x-6, bg-gray-700, rotate-45, border-green-500) that do not exist in the shipped CSS, and inline rgba gradients for the toggles. glass-max-h-80vh, glass-top-11 and glass-top-16 are also undefined.
motion: Uses framer-motion. Reduced motion is BROKEN: when prefersReducedMotion is true, the panel sets animate={} with initial {opacity:0, scale:0.9}, so it stays invisible (GlassA11y.tsx:399-402). Expanded sections stay at height 0 for the same reason (763-768). whileHover and whileTap scale effects ignore the OS reduced-motion preference.
a11y: The FAB has no aria-expanded or aria-controls. The tabs are buttons without the tablist/tab/aria-selected pattern. Several toggles (GlassHighContrast and GlassScreenReader switches) have no role='switch', no aria-checked and no label. The two header icon buttons have only a title, so they lack accessible names. The 'Detect system preferences' button has an empty onClick. The sr-only text 'Press Alt+A to open' advertises a shortcut that does not exist. The labels are not linked to their <select> elements by htmlFor or id. The panel hard-codes the claim 'WCAG 2.1 AAA Compliant'.
api: forwardRef, but className is concatenated without cn and there is no style passthrough. The props overlap (compact, preview and density='compact'; contained versus position). The config is internal 'mock' state (comment at line 152) and is not applied to the DOM or to any provider.
ssr: "use client". Imports framer-motion and the icon set. It does not access window during render.
fake_complexity: FAKE. 'Run Tests' waits on a setTimeout and returns hard-coded scores (95%, 100% and so on). The config changes nothing in the page. The section panels are created once inside useState with closures over the initial config, so the Settings tab always shows stale default values, and each toggle spreads the stale config, which resets the other settings.
target: if a preferences panel is wanted, a small GlassPreferencesPanel bound to the redesigned AccessibilityProvider
justification: It is 1,124 lines of demoware: mocked test results, a hard-coded AAA claim, a no-op detect button, an advertised shortcut that does not exist, stale-closure settings panels that reset each other, and a panel that becomes invisible under reduced motion. It is the opposite of what an accessibility component should be. Its look depends on Tailwind classes the library does not ship and on story-level !important overrides. Remove it, or rebuild a small honest preferences panel on top of a real provider.
evidence: src/components/accessibility/GlassA11y.tsx:399-402 (animate {} under reduced motion with initial opacity 0)

name: GlassHighContrast / GlassMotionControls / GlassScreenReader / GlassKeyboardNav (GlassA11y sub-panels)
stories: GlassA11y.stories.tsx: GlassKeyboardNav, GlassMotionControls (2); none for GlassHighContrast/GlassScreenReader
material_impl: Inline rgba gradients and box-shadows on the switch tracks and knobs (GlassMotionControls and GlassKeyboardNav). GlassHighContrast and GlassScreenReader use unprefixed Tailwind classes that are not shipped (w-12, h-6, bg-gray-700, translate-x-6), so their switches render unstyled.
a11y: This is inconsistent: GlassMotionControls and GlassKeyboardNav switches have role='switch' and aria-checked, while the GlassHighContrast and GlassScreenReader toggles are unlabeled buttons. The <label> elements are not linked to their selects.
api: config plus an updateConfig setter. They are not standalone, because they require the GlassA11yConfig shape.
fake_complexity: The toggles only mutate the config object, which affects nothing.
duplicates: GlassSwitch (root) should be used for every toggle
target: GlassSwitch/GlassSelect inside a rebuilt preferences panel
justification: These are internal pieces of a fake panel, leaked to the root export. They hand-roll switches instead of using GlassSwitch and have uneven a11y.

name: GlassFocusIndicators
stories: src/components/accessibility/GlassFocusIndicators.stories.tsx (6: Default, OutlineVariant, GlowVariant, HighContrast, DangerColor, AlwaysVisible). Five of them render identical markup with no differing props, so the story names are misleading.
tests: src/components/accessibility/GlassFocusIndicators.test.tsx. The tests are hollow: the focus tests query for focusable elements that never exist and pass vacuously inside if (element).
screenshots: reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification/screenshots/components-accessibility-glassfocusindicators/{desktop,mobile}.png (not renderable by the viewer; near-white, mean 243). The static capture cannot show a focus ring in any case.
material_impl: FocusRing relies on glass-position-fixed and glass-position-absolute, which are UNDEFINED, plus Tailwind ring classes that are not shipped (ring-3, ring-offset-2, ring-blue-400/60, bg-blue-400/8, -top-1). The 'fixed overlay' ring therefore renders as a static in-flow block where the component is mounted. Even if position:fixed applied, it adds window.scrollX and scrollY to viewport coordinates, which would double the offset when the page is scrolled. The imported CSS globally restyles every button, a, input and [tabindex] :focus-visible state (outline and box-shadow) as a side effect of importing the component.
motion: Framer-motion springs, an infinitely animated gradient border, and pulsing corner dots that run forever. Under reduced motion the ring is set to animate={} with initial opacity 0, so it is invisible.
a11y: Harmful side effects. It hijacks Alt+S, Alt+L and Alt+H globally (on macOS, Alt+L yields '¬', so that shortcut does not work there). Escape blurs any focused element document-wide, which can conflict with dialogs and menus. A 'focus trap' attaches keydown listeners to every [role=dialog], .modal and .overlay on each focus change and never removes them, so listeners leak and accumulate. It focuses landmarks and headings that are not focusable without tabindex, so those jumps silently fail. It calls an undefined window.announceToScreenReader. SkipLinks: .glass-sr-only (clip: rect(0,0,0,0)) is never undone on focus, because focus:glass-not-sr-only is undefined and .skip-link:focus does not reset clip. Skip links stay invisible when focused, which fails WCAG 2.4.7.
api: No props, ref or className. The global effect re-subscribes on every focus change because focusedElement is a dependency. Its companions SkipLinks, LandmarkAnnouncer and KeyboardShortcutsHelper are exported only through components/accessibility/index.ts.
ssr: "use client". The document and window listeners live in effects. The global CSS import is a side effect, which hurts tree-shaking and CSS order.
fake_complexity: Partially fake. The 'advanced animated focus rings' do not render as an overlay with the shipped CSS. Screen-reader announcements depend on a global function that does not exist.
justification: This component makes accessibility worse. It hijacks global shortcuts, blurs focus on Escape anywhere, leaks focus-trap listeners, restyles every focusable element through a side-effect CSS import, keeps skip links invisible when focused and hides its ring under reduced motion. Its overlay positioning classes do not exist. The primitives/focus folder already has proper SkipLinks and FocusTrap. A premium system needs one well-designed token :focus-visible ring in base CSS, not a JS-tracked overlay.
evidence: src/components/accessibility/GlassFocusIndicators.tsx:426-430 + src/styles/glass.css .glass-sr-only clip (skip link invisible on focus)
